Topic 2.2.1: Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you use MAKING leaner should be able to: • Guide learners to use one colour for painting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments
2. appreciate own and others painted work

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PAINTING MAKING TECHNIQUES
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PAINTING MAKING TECHNIQUES
Study Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments

What this means
In this part you learn to perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate own and others painted work

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate own and others painted work. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate own and others painted work.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate own and others painted work. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES in your own words. (skill: appreciate own and others painted work)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate own and others painted work.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you use MAKING leaner should be able to: • Guide learners to use one colour for painting?
2. What do you do • Guide learners to draw shape enjoyment • Guide learners to apply paint on shapes after painting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Painting MAKING TECHNIQUES means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform free choice using brushes painting on paper for • Display own painted work enjoyment • Guide learner to share comments.
5. Be able to: appreciate own and others painted work.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
